commits.message:
feat(parsing): split a numbered multi-position email into separate job requirement records

Real production email (jobs.nvoids.com relay): one recruiter posting
three distinct positions as a numbered list -- "1)Power Platform
Developer", "2 )Power BI Developer / BI Consultant", "3) PPM
Functional/Technical Consultant" -- rather than repeating a
"Job Title:" label per posting, the one format
_split_requirement_sections already handled. Produced a single garbled
record: job_title=None, required_skills mixing junk tokens pulled off
the footer URL ("https"), and the entire three-position block dumped
into one job_description. None of the three positions were extractable
as separate, postable requirements.

_numbered_position_sections (app/email_parsing/parsers.py) detects a
"N)" list starting at 1 with 2+ items and splits on it, the same way
the existing label-based splitter already does for repeated
"Job Title:" lines -- both now share _sections_from_matches. Bounded
against the email's own signoff marker (SIGNOFF_RE, reused from
app/email_parsing/signature.py) so the relay's boilerplate footer
("Keywords: ...", "View this job online", "Happy recruiting") never
gets absorbed into the last position's job_description. Each section's
title comes from its own first line (via extract_probable_title, same
extractor already used on the subject line) when there's no "Job Title:"
label to find.

A field one position states but another leaves out (location, most
commonly, when it's written once for the whole listing rather than
repeated under every item) is filled in from whichever position in the
same email did find it -- never for a single-record email, where a
missing field should surface as requires_review exactly as it always
has. When company gets filled in this way, confidence/warnings are
recomputed too (_score_requirement_record, factored out of the per-
section loop) rather than left stale from before the fill-forward ran.

apply_job_requirement_fallback (app/email_parsing/llm_fallback.py) now
skips outright for a multi-record result. It only ever patched
records[0] -- built for one job per email -- so a low-confidence multi-
position result was silently spending an LLM call to patch only the
first of several positions while leaving the rest exactly as
incomplete. Multi-position emails go to review as multiple honestly-
incomplete records instead.

New coverage: the exact production email splits into 3 correctly-
titled records with none of the relay's footer leaking into any of
them and the shared location filled into all three; a single position
whose own requirements happen to be numbered ("1) 5+ years Java")
does not falsely trigger a split; a multi-position result never
reaches the LLM fallback. Full regression suite (18 checks) green
against a fresh schema and rebuilt image.
